questions.stem:
Statements: No fish is a bird. Some birds can sing.

Conclusions: I. Some singers are birds. II. No fish can sing.
questions.explanation: I: 'Some birds can sing' ⟹ some singing-things are birds. TRUE. II: We only know fish ≠ birds; we don't know if any non-bird fish can sing. FALSE.

questions.stem: Five children stand in a line. P is between Q and R. S is to the immediate left of P. T is at the right end. The order from left is:
questions.explanation: P between Q and R, S immediately left of P, T at right end. Try Q, S, P, R, T: S is left of P ✓, P between... S and R (not Q and R). Try Q, P, R but S left of P means: Q, S, P, R — P is between S and R, not Q and R. Hmm. Let me redo: 'P is between Q and R' means Q and R are on either side of P, or just that P is between them in sequence. S immediately left of P. For arrangement, the only valid: Q, S, P, R, T — P is in the middle of Q and R (positions 2/3/4), S left of P. ✓
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If 1 March 2025 was a Saturday, what day was 1 March 2024?
questions.explanation: 2024 is leap year; Mar 2024 to Mar 2025 includes Feb 29. So 366 days. 366 mod 7 = 2 odd days. Going back 2 days from Saturday = Thursday. Hmm option (a) says Friday. Let me re-check: Mar 1, 2024 is leap-year-affected if we cross Feb 29. From Mar 1, 2024 to Mar 1, 2025 = exactly 365 days (Feb 29 of 2024 already happened by Mar 1, 2024). 365 mod 7 = 1. Going back 1 day from Saturday = Friday. So (a) Friday.
questions.subject: REASONING

Question: How is X related to Y?

Statement I: X is the brother of Y's father.
Statement II: X has only one nephew, Y.

questions.stem: How many Indians are expected to live in cities by 2030?
questions.passage_context: Urbanisation in India is accelerating at an unprecedented pace. By 2030, more than 600 million Indians are expected to live in cities. This shift brings both opportunities and challenges. Cities are engines of economic growth, contributing over 60% of GDP despite housing only a third of the population. Yet rapid urbanisation strains infrastructure: housing shortages, traffic congestion, water scarcity, and air pollution have all intensified. The Smart Cities Mission, launched in 2015, aims to retrofit and develop 100 cities with modern infrastructure and citizen-centric services. Progress varies widely. Cities like Indore have set examples in waste management and clean rankings, while many others struggle with implementation. Affordable housing, public transport, and inclusive urban planning will determine whether India's urban future becomes a story of broad-based prosperity or deepening inequality.
questions.explanation: Stated explicitly: 'more than 600 million Indians are expected to live in cities.'
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange and identify the FIRST sentence.

(A) The deal saved hundreds of jobs.
(B) Tata Steel acquired a struggling European mill in 2007.
(C) Initial scepticism gave way to operational improvements.
(D) Indian engineering teams were sent to overhaul processes.
(E) Today, the mill is profitable and competitive again.
questions.explanation: B (acquisition event) → C (initial reactions) → D (specific actions) → A (jobs saved) → E (current state). 1st = B.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange and identify the LAST sentence.

(A) Indian railways stretches across the entire country.
(B) It carries over 8 billion passengers annually.
(C) Modernisation efforts include electrification and high-speed corridors.
(D) Vande Bharat trains have set new benchmarks for speed and comfort.
(E) Future plans aim at full network electrification by 2030.
questions.explanation: A (intro) → B (scale) → C (modernisation) → D (Vande Bharat) → E (future). Last = E.
questions.subject: ENGLISH
